settings.tagline: Vintage American apparel featuring real family photographs and forgotten heritage designs. Every shirt has a story. Every story deserves to be worn.

settings.text: Every shirt tells a story. Our designs come from real family photographs spanning the 1920s-1990s and rare vintage logos from America's industrial era. This isn't manufactured nostalgia — it's history you can wear.

settings.title: THE FOREMAN TEE
settings.story: Carl made foreman at J&L Steel. Pittsburgh never forgot.

settings.title: SUNDAY DINNER TEE
settings.story: The Miller family. Twelve people. One table. Every Sunday.

settings.title: UNION LOCAL 47
settings.story: A badge from a union that built this country.

settings.title: THE ROAD TRIP TEE
settings.story: Route 66. A station wagon. Five kids. One summer.

settings.text: Tintype Thread Company started with a box of family photographs. Working-class Americans from the 1920s through the 1990s — factory workers, farmers, families at Sunday dinner. Their faces deserved more than a dusty album.

We’ve expanded to include rare vintage logos and designs from America’s industrial past — marks from companies long forgotten, badges from unions that built this country, graphics that tell the story of American labor.
Every design comes with its story. Because clothing should mean something.

settings.title: AUTHENTICITY
settings.description: Every photo is real. Every story is documented. No stock images, no manufactured heritage. Just real American history.

settings.title: QUALITY
settings.description: Premium fabrics, careful printing, made to last. We use USA-made cotton whenever possible because shortcuts aren’t in our vocabulary.

settings.title: PRESERVATION
settings.description: We’re building an archive of working-class American history, one design at a time. These stories deserve to survive.
